title: Hungarian Paprika Beef Stew with Egg Dumplings
summary: Hungarian pörkölt: chunks of beef braised slowly in their own juices with plenty of soft onions and sweet paprika, served with buttery egg dumplings and fresh green pepper rings.
equipment: large heavy casserole (Dutch oven, 5-6 litres) with lid
spaetzle maker or colander with large holes

ingredients.item: beef chuck, trimmed of excess fat, cut into 4 cm cubes
fine sea salt or table salt
green pepper (Hungarian wax or long sweet), sliced

ingredients.note: added a little at a time

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
green pepper (Hungarian wax or long sweet), sliced into thin rings, to serve

steps.title: Season the beef
steps.text: Sprinkle the beef cubes with the stew salt and set them aside while you cook the onions. Salting ahead gives it time to start seasoning the meat.

steps.title: Soften the onions
steps.text: Put the oil and onions in the casserole, cover and cook over medium-low heat for 10-12 minutes, stirring now and then, until very soft and golden but not browned. Add the garlic for 1 minute. These melted onions form the body of the sauce, thickening it without any flour.

steps.title: Add the paprika off the heat
steps.text: Take the pot off the heat and stir in both paprikas, the tomato purée and the caraway, then return it to low heat for 1 minute. Paprika burns and turns bitter in seconds over direct heat, so mixing it into the hot onions off the flame protects its sweet flavour and bright colour.

steps.title: Braise low and slow
steps.text: Add the beef, sliced pepper and tomato and stir to coat. Cover tightly and cook over low heat for 2 h-2 h 30 min, stirring every 20 minutes. The meat releases its own juices, so add water 50 ml at a time only if the pan looks dry; this keeps the sauce thick and concentrated rather than soupy.

steps.title: Check and finish
steps.text: The stew is ready when the beef is tender enough to cut with a spoon, as its tough connective tissue has melted into gelatine. Stir in the vinegar to lift the rich sauce.

steps.title: Mix the dumpling batter
steps.text: About 20 minutes before the stew is ready, bring the large saucepan of water to the boil. Beat the flour, eggs, cold water and dumpling salt into a thick, sticky batter that drops slowly from a spoon, then rest it for 10 minutes so the flour hydrates and the dumplings hold together.

steps.title: Cook the dumplings
steps.text: Press the batter through the spaetzle maker or colander into the simmering water in 2 batches. Cook for 2-3 minutes until they float, then lift them out with the slotted spoon and toss with the butter to stop them sticking.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon the stew onto plates with the dumplings and scatter over the green pepper rings for a fresh, crunchy contrast.

tips: A common mistake is adding paprika to a pan on the heat; it scorches almost instantly, so always take the pot off the heat first.
Resist adding lots of water: pörkölt should be thick, with just enough sauce to coat the meat and dumplings.
Use a good-quality sweet Hungarian paprika, as it provides most of the flavour.
If you have no spaetzle maker, scrape small pieces of batter off a wet chopping board into the water with a knife.
storage: Cool within 2 hours and refrigerate for up to 3 days; the stew also freezes well for up to 3 months. Reheat until piping hot (74 °C). The dumplings are best made fresh.
